# 1. Introduction: AELIX-002 transcriptome study description
  
This is the transcriptome (RNA-Seq) analysis of the AELIX-002 clinical trial. 
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-022-02060-2

**Timepoints Description**
  
* T01: Baseline, week 0 DDDMM/PPPPP regimen. First dose of DNA.HTI (D). 
* T02: Week 24 DDDMM/PPPPP regimen. Two weeks after second dose of MVA.HTI (M).
* T03: Baseline, week 0 CCM/PPP regimen. First dose of ChAdOx1.HTI (C).
* T04: Week 16 CCM/PPP regimen. Four weeks after second dose of ChAdOx1.HTI (C).
* T05: Week 32 CCM/PPP regimen. Antiretroviral treatmen interruption (ATI) start.  

**Participants Description**
  
From the 45 participants of the study, 41 completed the vaccination regimen. Moreover:
  
* 38 participants with 5 timepoints (w0 and w24 DDDMM/PPPPP regimen, W0, w16, and w32 CCM/PPP regimen).
* Participant 11 (Vax) with 4 timepoints (w24 DDDMM missing, nordre: 2018030085).
* Participant 20 (Pbo) with 4 timepoints (w24 PPPPP missing, nordre: 2018110220).
* Participant 49 (Vax) with 3 timepoints (w16 and w32 CCM missing, nordre: 2019090082 and 2020010006, respectively).
* Participants with beneficial alleles: 13, 19, 22, 27, 30, and 31 (vax), 16, 17, and 36 (Pbo) were excluded for this analysis.
* Participant 01 was removed because is the only woman in the study.

# 2. Transcriptome analysis - Data Normalization and Exploration

# 2.1. Data Pre-processing

```{r libraries, include = F, warning=F}
library(limma)
library(edgeR)
library(sva)
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
library(gridExtra)
library(knitr)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(mixOmics)
library(dplyr)
library(dendextend)
library(gplots)
library(VennDiagram)
library(tidyr)
library(DOSE)
library(GO.db)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(GSEABase)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(biomaRt)
library(Mfuzz)
library(ggrepel)
library(reshape)
library(ggpubr)
library(readxl)
```

```{r load datasets}
# Matrix of read counts
data <- read_excel("Read_counts.xlsx")
# Informations of participants
info <- read.csv2("Info_sample.csv")
# Selecting only the counts
counts <- data[, 12:162]
# Creating rownames for counts dataframe
rownames(counts) <- paste(data$Transcript_ID , data$Gene_Symbol, data$Description) 
```


# 2.2. Data Normalization

The normalization method Trimmed Mean of M values (TMM) accounts for sequencing depth, 
RNA composition and gene length. This normalization function is from the R package edge R

```{r Data Normalization}
info$npac <- as.factor(info$npac)
y <- DGEList(counts = counts) 
# Object from a table of counts (rows=features, columns=samples), group indicator for each 
# column, library size (optional) and a table of feature annotation (optional).
isexpr <- rowSums(cpm(y) > 1) >= 5 
# Compute counts per million and take those genes that have at least 1 count in 5 of the samples. 
y <- y[isexpr, keep.lib.size = FALSE]
y <- calcNormFactors(y) 
# Apply the scale normalization that by default is TMM. 
save(y, file = "TMMcounts.RData")
```

# 2.3 Voom transformation
```{r}
voom_counts1 <- voom(y, design = NULL)
hist(voom_counts1$E)
voom_counts <- voom_counts1$E
write.table(voom_counts, file ="Log2NormalizedCounts.txt")
save(y, info, voom_counts, file = "DataRNA_filterIND.RData")
```


# 3. Exploratory Data Analysis

# 3.1. Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

PCA on log2 normalized data

```{r, PCA log2 Normalized Data}
# Run the method
MyResult_PCA <- pca(t(voom_counts))  
MyResult_PCA2 <- pca(t(voom_counts), ncomp = 4)   # using 4 components

# Plot the samples according to different variables (components 1 and 2)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$Time2, centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)  
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA, group = info$Treat, centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)  
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA, group = info$Resumption, centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA, group = info$Cri1, centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA, group = info$Cri2, centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA, group = info$Cri3, centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA, group = info$Cri4, centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA, group = info$npac, centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)

# Plot the samples according to different variables (components 1 and 4)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$Time2,  comp = c(1,4), centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)  
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$Treat, comp = c(1,4), centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)  
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$Resumption, comp = c(1,4), centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$Cri1, comp = c(1,4), centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$Cri2, comp = c(1,4), centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$Cri3, comp = c(1,4), centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$Cri4, comp = c(1,4), centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
plotIndiv(MyResult_PCA2, group = info$npac, comp = c(1,4), centre = FALSE, ellipse = FALSE, legend = TRUE)
```

# 4. Transcriptome Analysis - Differential Expression Analysis

The first endpoint is try to identify the molecular mechanisms involved in the different time points. 

It is necessary to apply the voom function to apply limma in RNA-Seq: Transform count data to log2-counts per million (logCPM) estimate the mean-variance relationship use this to compute appropriate observation-level weights. The data are then ready for linear modelling. We include a correlation structure between the individuals: duplicateCorrelation

# 4.1. Design - Week

```{r, limma, warning = FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
load("../RNASeq/DataRNA_filterIND.RData")
npac <- factor(info$npac)
length(levels(npac)) # 31 participants
Time <- factor(info$Time2)
levels(Time) <- c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4", "T5")
mod1 <- model.matrix(~0 + Time)
colnames(mod1)= c(levels(Time))
contr.matrix1 <- makeContrasts(
  T1vsT2 = T2 - T1,
  T1vsT3 = T3 - T1,
  T1vsT4 = T4 - T1,
  T1vsT5 = T5 - T1,
  T2vsT3 = T3 - T2,
  T2vsT4 = T4 - T2,
  T2vsT5 = T5 - T2,
  T3vsT4 = T4 - T3,
  T3vsT5 = T5 - T3,
  T4vsT5 = T5 - T4,
  levels=colnames(mod1))

# Model
# Since AELIX-002 is a longitudinal study, we add information of the individual. 
cor1 <- duplicateCorrelation(voom_counts, mod1, block = npac)
fit <- lmFit(voom_counts, mod1, block = npac, correlation = cor1$consensus)

# Simple comparison
fit1 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts = contr.matrix1)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit1)
summary(decideTests(fit2))
dir.create("../Analyses/DEGtimepoints")
dir.create("../Analyses/DEGtimepoints/LimmaBlock")
write.table(summary(decideTests(fit2)), file = "../Analyses/DEGtimepoints/SummaryRes.txt", sep = "\t")
for (i in  colnames(fit2$coefficients)){
  toptable1 <- topTable(fit2, coef = i, sort = "p", n = Inf, adjust = "BH",  resort.by = "p")
  write.table(toptable1, sep = ";", paste(paste("../Analyses/DEGtimepoints/LimmaBlock", i), ".txt", sep = ""), quote = F)
  toptable2 <- topTable(fit2, coef = i, sort = "p", n = Inf, adjust = "BH",  resort.by = "p", p.value = 0.2)
  write.table(toptable2, sep = ";", paste(paste("../Analyses/DEGtimepoints/LimmaBlock/qval", i), ".txt", sep = ""), quote = F)
}
```
